input: Request a flexible working arrangement from my employer

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Flexible working covers many arrangements — remote work, reduced hours, compressed weeks, flexi-time, job sharing — and the specific type completely changes what the request should say and how it should be justified.
Whether the user is making a formal statutory request, an informal conversation with a line manager, or going through HR changes the tone, format, and formality required.
The user's current work setup (fully office-based, hybrid, industry type) and how long they've been employed affects what they're entitled to and what arguments will land.
A hard deadline — such as a return from parental leave, a health need, or a childcare start date — determines how urgently the request needs to be submitted and processed.
The reason behind the request (childcare, health, side project, commute, wellbeing) shapes the most persuasive justification to include and what tone is appropriate.
Knowing what outcome the user needs vs. what they'd accept as a compromise determines how firm or flexible to be in the request, and what a successful result looks like.
Whether the user needs help writing a formal letter, preparing for a conversation, or building a business case determines the concrete deliverable to produce.

gold.taskTitle: Request a flexible working arrangement from employer
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to formally request a flexible working arrangement from their employer, covering the type of flexibility sought, the rationale, and how to approach the process effectively.

questions.title: What type of flexibility are you asking for?
questions.description: Identify the specific arrangement being requested — e.g. fully remote, reduced hours, compressed 4-day week, flexi-start/finish times, or hybrid split.

questions.title: Who will you be submitting this request to?
questions.description: Clarify whether the request is directed to a line manager informally, submitted formally to HR, or filed as a statutory flexible working request.

questions.title: What is your current working setup and employment situation?
questions.description: Understand the user's current arrangement (fully office-based, hybrid, etc.), their industry, and how long they have been employed — all of which affect eligibility and framing.

questions.title: Is there a specific date by which this needs to be in place?
questions.description: Determine whether there is a hard deadline driving the request, such as a childcare arrangement, health condition start date, or return from leave.

questions.title: What is your main reason for wanting this arrangement?
questions.description: Identify the personal driver behind the request — childcare, a health or disability need, long commute, wellbeing, or a personal project — to shape the most compelling justification.

questions.title: What outcome would you consider a success here?
questions.description: Establish whether the user needs the exact arrangement they are requesting, or whether there are acceptable compromises — this determines how firm or negotiable the request should be.

questions.title: What do you need as the end deliverable for this task?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs a written formal request letter, a business case document, a conversation script, or step-by-step guidance on the process.
